tools.name: identify_patient
tools.description: When to call this tool: the caller may already be a patient and you need to find their chart before verify_identity. What it does: looks up masked candidates, trying the number they are calling from first. This does not verify identity. When another tool is better: call verify_identity once you have a name and date of birth; call get_patient_summary only after verification succeeds.

dob.description: Calendar date YYYY-MM-DD. No time, no timezone.

tools.name: verify_identity
tools.description: When to call this tool: you have the caller's name and date of birth and must confirm they are the patient before any protected chart work. What it does: spends one verification attempt; add zip or last four of the phone on file only if a prior lookup asked for a second factor. After three failures this locks. Never ask for a Social Security number. When another tool is better: call identify_patient first if you do not yet have a chart match; call get_patient_summary immediately after this succeeds.

full_name.description: Full legal name, given name then family name.

dob.description: Calendar date YYYY-MM-DD. No time, no timezone.

second_factor.description: ZIP (5 digits) or last four of the phone on file.

tools.name: get_patient_summary
tools.description: When to call this tool: identity verification just succeeded — load the chart before handing off or starting specialist work. What it does: returns home office, upcoming appointments, insurance on file, balance, portal status, and open orders. Identity-gated. When another tool is better: get_account_balance for a live bill amount; get_results_status for result STATUS; find_slots for open times. Do not call this unverified.

tools.name: list_locations
tools.description: When to call this tool: the caller asks for an office address, floor, suite, hours, parking, or transit; names an office; or you need an office id before booking or a coverage check. What it does: the only source of address, floor, suite, hours, parking, transit, services, and location ids. Never guess. When another tool is better: quote_cosmetic_service for a price; check_plan_accepted for whether a plan is taken at that office; find_slots for appointment times.

location_id.description: Office id. Map caller names: Park Avenue → loc_park_ave, Brooklyn Heights → loc_brooklyn_heights, Windermere → loc_windermere.

tools.name: classify_visit_request
tools.description: When to call this tool: the caller described a medical, surgical, or allergy reason for a visit and you need the appointment type before searching slots. What it does: maps the complaint to type and credential so a Mohs consult is never booked with a PA. Always call this before find_slots for medical, Mohs, or allergy visits. When another tool is better: quote_cosmetic_service and book_cosmetic_consult for Botox, fillers, peels, or lasers — never classify those here. schedule_allergy_service for a named allergy service after they already have an allergy evaluation.

visit_class.description: Closed visit class. mohs = skin cancer / Mohs; allergy = hives/testing/shots eval; medical = everything else. Cosmetic visits are not classified here.

is_new_patient.description: True if they have never been seen at Straus.

urgency.description: urgent for spreading, painful, bleeding, or infected complaints; routine otherwise.

tools.name: find_slots
tools.description: When to call this tool: you are ready to offer appointment times at specific offices. Call after classify_visit_request for medical visits, or when booking a cosmetic consult after quote_cosmetic_service. What it does: returns open slots for the given office ids. Offer two or three; never promise a time this did not return. When another tool is better: schedule_allergy_service for a dedicated allergy service (skin testing, shots, patch testing) — that tool picks the slot. list_locations for address or hours.

items.description: Office id. Map caller names: Park Avenue → loc_park_ave, Brooklyn Heights → loc_brooklyn_heights, Windermere → loc_windermere.

location_ids.description: One or more office ids to search.

window_start.description: Inclusive search bound at minute precision. YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM. No seconds, no timezone. Example: 2026-08-24T09:00. Omit if they did not name a start. Do not invent midnight.

window_end.description: Inclusive search bound at minute precision. YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM. No seconds, no timezone. The selected slot, including duration, must end by this time. Omit if they did not name an end.

tools.name: book_appointment
tools.description: When to call this tool: the caller said yes after you read back the day, time, office with floor, and provider with credentials for a medical, Mohs, or allergy evaluation visit. What it does: creates that appointment. Slot fields must match the find_slots offer. When another tool is better: book_cosmetic_consult for a cosmetic consult; schedule_allergy_service for a named allergy service; reschedule_appointment to move an existing visit.

appointment_type_code.description: Appointment type code from classify_visit_request. Never COS_CONSULT — use book_cosmetic_consult.

location_id.description: Office id. Map caller names: Park Avenue → loc_park_ave, Brooklyn Heights → loc_brooklyn_heights, Windermere → loc_windermere.

provider_id.description: Provider id from find_slots or get_patient_summary: prov_chen, prov_ruiz, or prov_patel.

start.description: Local wall time at minute precision. YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM. No seconds, no timezone. Example: 2026-08-24T09:00. Open slots exist at :00 and :30 only.

end.description: Local wall time at minute precision. YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM. No seconds, no timezone. Example: 2026-08-24T09:00. Open slots exist at :00 and :30 only.

tools.name: reschedule_appointment
tools.description: When to call this tool: the caller wants to move an existing appointment — offer this before cancelling. What it does: updates the booking to a new slot. Moving never costs anything; say so. Identity-gated to their own bookings. When another tool is better: cancel_appointment if they still want the visit dropped after you offered a move; find_slots first to pick the new time.

appointment_id.description: Appointment id as a decimal string, e.g. "1".

new_start.description: Local wall time at minute precision. YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM. No seconds, no timezone. Example: 2026-08-24T09:00. Open slots exist at :00 and :30 only.

new_end.description: Local wall time at minute precision. YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM. No seconds, no timezone. Example: 2026-08-24T09:00. Open slots exist at :00 and :30 only.

tools.name: cancel_appointment
tools.description: When to call this tool: they still want to cancel after you offered to move the visit instead. What it does: first call without fee acceptance; if a fee applies, say the exact wording returned, offer a different time, and only call again after they accept. Identity-gated. When another tool is better: reschedule_appointment if they will take another time; join_waitlist after a cancel if they want an earlier opening later.

appointment_id.description: Appointment id as a decimal string, e.g. "1".

cancellation_reason_code.description: Why the visit is being cancelled.

fee_disclosed_and_accepted.description: False on the first call. True only after they accepted the spoken fee.

tools.name: join_waitlist
tools.description: When to call this tool: they want an earlier opening than the slots you can offer, or they decline to rebook after a cancel. What it does: puts them on the earlier-appointment list for the given type and offices. When another tool is better: find_slots and book_appointment if an open time already works; reschedule_appointment to move a booked visit.

appointment_type_code.description: Appointment type for the earlier opening. Cosmetic consults are not waitlisted here.

items.description: Office id. Map caller names: Park Avenue → loc_park_ave, Brooklyn Heights → loc_brooklyn_heights, Windermere → loc_windermere.

location_ids.description: Offices they will take an earlier opening at.

earliest.description: Calendar date YYYY-MM-DD. No time. They named dates only — do not invent a clock time.

latest.description: Calendar date YYYY-MM-DD. No time. They named dates only — do not invent a clock time.

tools.name: schedule_allergy_service
tools.description: When to call this tool: book a dedicated allergy service (skin testing, patch testing, shots, and the like) after an explicit yes. What it does: picks the first available slot in office hours inside the optional search window. Call once after acceptance; repeats return the existing booking. Say prep, observation time, and linked return visits out loud. When another tool is better: find_slots and book_appointment for a new-patient or follow-up allergy evaluation visit; classify_visit_request first when they still need that evaluation appointment type.

location_id.description: Office id. Map caller names: Park Avenue → loc_park_ave, Brooklyn Heights → loc_brooklyn_heights, Windermere → loc_windermere.

window_start.description: Inclusive search bound at minute precision. YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM. No seconds, no timezone. Example: 2026-08-24T09:00. Omit if they did not name a start. Do not invent midnight.

window_end.description: Inclusive search bound at minute precision. YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM. No seconds, no timezone. The selected slot, including duration, must end by this time. Omit if they did not name an end.

tools.name: check_plan_accepted
tools.description: When to call this tool: the caller asks whether you take a plan at a specific office. You must call this; do not answer from the prompt. What it does: returns office-specific (and sometimes provider-specific) acceptance. If must_not_assert is true, say required_script and do not claim covered or not. When another tool is better: run_eligibility_check when they want a live copay, deductible, or coinsurance and have given a member ID; capture_insurance_update to put a new card on file; list_locations if you do not yet have an office id.

carrier.description: Payer slug. Map caller names: Aetna → aetna, UnitedHealthcare → unitedhealthcare, Blue Cross → bcbs, Oscar Health → oscar_health, Medicaid → medicaid. Unknown payers → other.

location_id.description: Office id. Map caller names: Park Avenue → loc_park_ave, Brooklyn Heights → loc_brooklyn_heights, Windermere → loc_windermere.

provider_id.description: Provider id from find_slots or get_patient_summary: prov_chen, prov_ruiz, or prov_patel.

tools.name: run_eligibility_check
tools.description: When to call this tool: they want a live copay, deductible, or coinsurance and have given a member ID. What it does: queries the payer for benefit numbers on a service date. If the payer does not answer, say you could not get the number — never guess a copay. When another tool is better: check_plan_accepted for whether the office takes the plan at all; capture_insurance_update to save a new card. Do not call this without a member ID.

carrier.description: Payer slug. Map caller names: Aetna → aetna, UnitedHealthcare → unitedhealthcare, Blue Cross → bcbs, Oscar Health → oscar_health, Medicaid → medicaid. Unknown payers → other.

member_id.description: Member or subscriber id, letters and digits only.

dob.description: Calendar date YYYY-MM-DD. No time, no timezone.

service_date.description: Calendar date YYYY-MM-DD. No time, no timezone.

tools.name: capture_insurance_update
tools.description: When to call this tool: they have new or changed insurance to put on file. Carrier plus member ID is enough. What it does: saves those fields and texts a secure link for card photos. Never ask for a Social Security number. Identity-gated. When another tool is better: check_plan_accepted to answer 'do you take this plan'; run_eligibility_check for a live copay. Do not use send_sms for the card-photo link — this tool sends it.

carrier.description: Payer slug. Map caller names: Aetna → aetna, UnitedHealthcare → unitedhealthcare, Blue Cross → bcbs, Oscar Health → oscar_health, Medicaid → medicaid. Unknown payers → other.

member_id.description: Member or subscriber id, letters and digits only.

group_number.description: Group number, letters and digits only.

subscriber_relationship.description: Who the subscriber is relative to the patient.

tools.name: get_account_balance
tools.description: When to call this tool: they ask about a bill, balance, or charge — call this first, before explaining or collecting. What it does: returns the current balance and line items. Identity-gated; do not invent a sample amount. When another tool is better: explain_charge for why a specific line exists; send_payment_link when they are ready to pay; request_fee_waiver to queue a missed-visit fee review.

tools.name: explain_charge
tools.description: When to call this tool: they ask why a specific charge is on the account. What it does: returns approved_script for that line. Say it as written — do not improvise a billing explanation. Identity-gated. When another tool is better: get_account_balance first if you do not yet have the lines; request_fee_waiver if they dispute a missed-visit fee after hearing the script.

tools.name: send_payment_link
tools.description: When to call this tool: they are ready to pay a medical balance or a cosmetic deposit. What it does: texts a secure payment link — the only payment path; never take a card by voice. When another tool is better: offer_financing when they cannot pay the full amount at once and the amount is over two hundred fifty dollars; send_sms only for an appointment confirmation after booking.

tools.name: offer_financing
tools.description: When to call this tool: they cannot pay the full amount at once and the balance or quoted amount is over two hundred fifty dollars. What it does: offers CareCredit. Do not offer it for smaller amounts. Pass amount_cents when they named a number; otherwise this uses the last quote low end or account balance already loaded. When another tool is better: send_payment_link when they will pay now; quote_cosmetic_service for the price itself.

tools.name: request_fee_waiver
tools.description: When to call this tool: they dispute a missed-visit fee and want it reviewed. What it does: queues a review. You do not waive it yourself — say the SLA the tool returns out loud. When another tool is better: explain_charge first so they hear why the fee is there; cancel_appointment if the fee has not been posted yet and they still need the visit cancelled.

fee_line_item_id.description: Missed-visit fee line only. Visit balances are not waived here.

tools.name: quote_cosmetic_service
tools.description: When to call this tool: they ask what a cosmetic treatment costs. What it does: the only source of a spoken cosmetic price. If it returns a range, say that range and that the consult settles the number; if no range, never invent one. When another tool is better: book_cosmetic_consult when they are ready to book the consult; list_locations if they only asked whether an office offers cosmetic work.

tools.name: book_cosmetic_consult
tools.description: When to call this tool: they are ready to book a cosmetic consult. First call without policy acknowledgment returns four policy lines — say them verbatim, get a real yes, then call again with acknowledgment. What it does: books the cosmetic consult after policy yes. Do not book before that yes. When another tool is better: book_appointment for medical, Mohs, or allergy evaluation visits; quote_cosmetic_service before you have given a price; find_slots to pick the time.

service_interest.description: Cosmetic services they want discussed at the consult.

location_id.description: Office id. Map caller names: Park Avenue → loc_park_ave, Brooklyn Heights → loc_brooklyn_heights, Windermere → loc_windermere.

provider_id.description: Provider id from find_slots or get_patient_summary: prov_chen, prov_ruiz, or prov_patel.

start.description: Local wall time at minute precision. YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM. No seconds, no timezone. Example: 2026-08-24T09:00. Open slots exist at :00 and :30 only.

policy_acknowledged.description: False on the first call. True only after they accepted the four policy lines.

tools.name: request_rx_refill
tools.description: When to call this tool: immediately after identity verification for any named-medication refill or refill-related prior authorization, before policy talk, extra details, a clinical message, callback, or handoff. What it does: records and routes the refill. medication_name is the only input. Never approves. Follow the returned route. When another tool is better: create_clinical_message after this write if they also need a nurse callback; transfer to scheduling if the route says they need a visit first. This message never replaces this refill request.

medication_name.description: Closed formulary slug, lowercase. Map spoken names: Accutane → accutane, Dupixent → dupixent, Xanax → xanax, isotretinoin → isotretinoin.

tools.name: get_results_status
tools.description: When to call this tool: they ask about pathology, lab, or allergy testing results. What it does: returns STATUS only, never the content. Say approved_script; if they push for what the results say, hold the line and create a clinical message instead. When another tool is better: create_clinical_message when they want result content you cannot read, or when status is back-but-not-released; send_portal_activation when results are released and the portal is inactive.

order_type.description: Which kind of result they are asking about.

tools.name: create_clinical_message
tools.description: When to call this tool: a nurse, results, or refill question needs the clinical team — including when they push for result content you cannot read. What it does: files an identity-gated clinical inbox message and returns a callback window. Say that window out loud. When another tool is better: request_rx_refill first for any named-medication refill — this message never replaces that write; create_callback_task for a non-clinical team callback; get_results_status for status before you message about results.

priority.description: stat for anything emergent, urgent otherwise, routine for results follow-up.

tools.name: send_sms
tools.description: When to call this tool: they asked for an appointment confirmation text after a medical booking, reschedule, or allergy service was just committed. What it does: sends the appointment_confirmation template only. Never free-form text. When another tool is better: send_payment_link for a payment or deposit; send_portal_activation for portal access; capture_insurance_update for a card-photo link; list_locations for spoken directions. Do not use this for those.

tools.name: send_portal_activation
tools.description: When to call this tool: the portal is not active and they need access — on every results call where it is inactive, before the call ends. What it does: sends the activation link by sms or email. When another tool is better: get_results_status for result STATUS; send_sms only for appointment confirmation. Do not use send_sms for portal activation.

channel.description: Delivery channel for the activation link.

tools.name: create_callback_task
tools.description: When to call this tool: you need to promise a callback with a real tracked SLA — after a tool cannot finish the work, or they need a team to call back. What it does: creates a queued callback. Say spoken_commitment out loud, verbatim. When another tool is better: do not use this instead of a tool that already has the answer. create_clinical_message for a clinical-team inbox item with a callback window; transfer_to_human if they asked for a person.

priority.description: Callback SLA. routine is the default.

tools.name: transfer_to_identity
tools.description: When to call this tool: chart access is required before the real work — existing-patient scheduling, billing, clinical, updating insurance on file, or an existing-patient cosmetic request. What it does: an invisible hop to identity. Pass next_intent so identity knows where to continue after verification. Do not announce it. When another tool is better: transfer_to_scheduling, transfer_to_coverage, or transfer_to_cosmetic directly when the caller is new and nothing protected is needed yet.

next_intent.description: Where identity should continue after verification.

tools.name: transfer_to_scheduling
tools.description: When to call this tool: the remaining work is booking, moving, cancelling, waitlist, or an allergy evaluation visit. What it does: an invisible hop to scheduling. No arguments. Do not announce it. When another tool is better: transfer_to_cosmetic for Botox, fillers, peels, lasers, or a cosmetic consult; transfer_to_coverage if the live question is still plan acceptance or eligibility.

tools.name: transfer_to_coverage
tools.description: When to call this tool: the question is plan acceptance, a referral, eligibility, or capturing a new insurance card. What it does: an invisible hop to coverage. No arguments. Do not announce it. When another tool is better: transfer_to_scheduling once coverage is settled and they want to book; transfer_to_identity first when an existing patient needs a card saved on file.

tools.name: transfer_to_cosmetic
tools.description: When to call this tool: they want Botox, fillers, lasers, peels, cosmetic pricing, or a cosmetic consult. What it does: an invisible hop to cosmetic. No arguments. Do not announce it. When another tool is better: transfer_to_scheduling for medical, Mohs, or allergy visits; list_locations if they only asked whether a named office offers cosmetic work.

tools.name: transfer_to_billing
tools.description: When to call this tool: the remaining work is a balance, charge explanation, payment, financing, or a fee waiver. Caller must already be identity-verified. What it does: an invisible hop to billing. No arguments. Do not announce it. When another tool is better: transfer_to_identity first if they are not yet verified; send_payment_link is billing's own tool, not a reason to hop elsewhere.

tools.name: transfer_to_clinical
tools.description: When to call this tool: the remaining work is results status, a refill, a nurse message, prior auth, portal, or records. Caller must already be identity-verified. What it does: an invisible hop to clinical. No arguments. Do not announce it. When another tool is better: transfer_to_identity first if they are not yet verified; transfer_to_scheduling if the remaining work is only booking a visit.

tools.name: transfer_to_human
tools.description: When to call this tool: the caller asks for a person, or you have told them to call 911 and said you are transferring them for a clinical emergency. What it does: the only transfer you announce out loud. Ends the voice-agent path. When another tool is better: not for hard questions, policy limits, or a slow call. create_callback_task if they need a team to call back and did not ask for a person.

reason.description: Why this is leaving the voice agent.

tools.name: end_call
tools.description: When to call this tool: the caller is done — say goodbye first — or this is spam or a wrong number. What it does: ends the session. A finished call after goodbye is caller_done; there is no silent-hangup reason. When another tool is better: transfer_to_human if they asked for a person or this is a clinical emergency after the 911 lines.
